title: Entropy-based Attention Regularization Frees Unintended Bias Mitigation from Lists
measurement_description: The paper measures unintended bias in hate speech detection models against various identity groups, including religious ones. It evaluates whether models incorrectly classify non-hateful text as hate speech due to the presence of specific religious identity terms (e.g., 'Muslim', 'Jewish').
findings: The proposed knowledge-free method, Entropy-based Attention Regularization (EAR), when applied to BERT (BERT+EAR), effectively mitigates unintended bias against identity terms, including religious ones. It reduces the model's tendency to overfit on these terms, leading to fairer and more accurate hate speech detection without requiring a predefined list of sensitive terms.
